title: Use AI tools to learn product management, carefully
summary: AI assistants can explain ideas, critique your writing and act as a practice partner. They can also be confidently wrong. Use them to speed up learning, never to replace your own thinking or your own evidence.

beginner: Choose one assistant you can use freely. Read the guidance on writing clear prompts in the sources, which works for any tool, and note three tips.
Ask it to explain a concept you are learning, such as a funnel, in plain English with an example. Check the explanation against one of the sources in this plan.
Ask for a critique. Paste a short piece you wrote, such as a problem statement, and ask what is unclear or missing. Decide yourself which comments to accept.
Use it as a practice partner. Ask it to play an interviewer and ask follow-up questions about a decision you describe. Answer out loud.
Test its limits. Ask for a statistic or a quote, then try to find the original. Note what it got wrong.
Never paste in private or confidential information, such as your employer's documents, customer data or other people's personal details. Use made-up or public examples.
Write three rules for how you will use AI while learning, for example 'I check facts against a source' and 'I write the first draft myself'.

toolExamples.claude: Ask it to explain a concept and to list what it is unsure about. Then check one claim in a source.
toolExamples.chatgpt: Ask it to act as an interviewer for a product role and to give you one thing to improve after each answer.
toolExamples.gemini: Ask it to critique a short problem statement and to point out missing evidence.

definitionOfDone: Three rules for using AI written down
One concept checked against a source
One critique of your own writing reviewed
pitfalls: Letting the tool write your practice work, so you learn nothing
Pasting in confidential or personal information
